chapters.title: The Medieval T-O Map
chapters.tease: A circle, a T and three continents taught Europe for a thousand years that a map can state a belief.

chapters.title: Ptolemy's Coordinate Grid
chapters.tease: Ptolemy gave every place on earth an address of two numbers, and the grid outlived every map drawn on it.

chapters.title: The Hereford Mappa Mundi
chapters.tease: One calfskin held scripture, myth and geography together: an encyclopaedia you could stand in front of.

chapters.title: Waldseemüller's 1507 Map
chapters.tease: A woodcut world map printed one new word on a new continent, and the name America never came off.

chapters.title: The Mercator Projection
chapters.tease: A grid built for sailors made every compass course a straight line, and quietly made Europe look enormous.

chapters.title: Cassini's Triangulation of France
chapters.tease: Four generations of Cassinis covered France in measured triangles, making the first modern national map.

chapters.title: William Smith's Geological Map
chapters.tease: A surveyor's hand-coloured map showed what lies beneath a whole country and made geology useful.

chapters.title: Beck's London Tube Map
chapters.tease: An off-duty draughtsman threw away geography, and invented the way the world reads its railways.

chapters.title: Tharp's Map of the Ocean Floor
chapters.tease: Barred from the ships, Marie Tharp drew the sea floor from soundings and found the rift at its heart.

chapters.title: The Peters Projection
chapters.tease: A map with honest areas and ugly shapes turned cartography into a public argument about power.

chapters.title: Ptolemy's Epicycles
chapters.tease: Circles riding on circles kept Earth at the centre of the heavens, and predicted the planets, for 1,400 years.

chapters.title: Copernicus's Heliocentric Sketch
chapters.tease: Moving one dot from Earth to the Sun redrew the cosmos and demoted humanity from the centre of creation.

chapters.title: Newton's Prism Experiment
chapters.tease: A beam through a shutter hole proved that white light is a mixture, and that colour belongs to light itself.

chapters.title: Newton's Cannonball
chapters.tease: A cannon on an impossibly tall mountain showed that an orbit is simply falling while missing the ground.

chapters.title: Mendeleev's Periodic Table
chapters.tease: A table with deliberate gaps predicted elements nobody had seen, and gave all of chemistry its order.

chapters.title: Minkowski's Light Cone
chapters.tease: Time as an axis, light at 45 degrees: one drawing made relativity geometry and fixed the limits of cause.

chapters.title: The Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram
chapters.tease: Plotting stars by brightness against colour revealed a hidden diagonal: the life story of every star.

chapters.title: Bohr's Model of the Atom
chapters.tease: Electrons on fixed rungs, leaping between them, explained hydrogen's colours and opened the quantum age.

chapters.title: Hubble's Expanding Universe
chapters.tease: Two dozen galaxies on one scatter plot showed that the farther away they are, the faster they recede.

chapters.title: The Feynman Diagram
chapters.tease: Squiggles and arrows turned the hardest sums in physics into pictures that are also calculations.

chapters.title: Vesalius's Fabrica Plates
chapters.tease: Anatomy stopped trusting the ancient textbook and started trusting the body on the table.

chapters.title: Harvey's Valve Experiment
chapters.tease: A tied arm and a pressing finger proved that blood circulates, and overturned Galen once more.

chapters.title: Linnaeus's Ranked Kingdoms
chapters.tease: A nested ladder of ranks and, later, a two-word name gave all of life one shared filing system.

chapters.title: Darwin's 'I Think' Tree
chapters.tease: Two hesitant words above a scribbled tree replaced the ladder of life with a branching family.

chapters.title: Gray's Anatomy Plates
chapters.tease: Carter's labelled engravings put the name on the bone and taught generations of doctors to see.

chapters.title: Haeckel's Tree of Life
chapters.tease: Haeckel drew evolution's first great family tree of all life, and quietly put humanity on top.

chapters.title: The Punnett Square
chapters.tease: Four boxes turned the mystery of heredity into a sum that any schoolchild can do.

chapters.title: The Krebs Cycle
chapters.tease: Respiration turned out to be a wheel, and the wheel turned out to run almost all complex life.

chapters.title: The DNA Double Helix
chapters.tease: One sketch of two twisting ribbons revealed how life copies itself, and began the age of genetics.

chapters.title: Crick's Central Dogma
chapters.tease: Crick's arrows fixed the direction of life's information flow, DNA to RNA to protein, and never back.

chapters.title: Euclid's Windmill Proof
chapters.tease: A right triangle and three squares turned measurement into proof, and taught the world what proving means.

chapters.title: Pascal's Triangle
chapters.tease: One rule, add the two numbers above, built a table that founded probability and runs through mathematics.

chapters.title: Descartes' Coordinate Plane
chapters.tease: Two crossed lines turned shapes into equations and equations into shapes, and every graph since sits on them.

chapters.title: The Bridges of Königsberg
chapters.tease: Euler shrank a city to dots and lines to prove a walk impossible, and graph theory was born.

chapters.title: The Bell Curve
chapters.tease: One smooth curve became the shape of chance, error and the average, from coin tosses to quality control.

chapters.title: The Argand Plane
chapters.tease: Drawing imaginary numbers at right angles to real ones made them ordinary, and powered electrical engineering.

chapters.title: The Venn Diagram
chapters.tease: Circles showing every possibility before any fact made logic visible, and became everyone's favourite diagram.

chapters.title: Cantor's Diagonal Argument
chapters.tease: A grid of symbols with one diagonal changed proved that some infinities are bigger than others.

chapters.title: Lorenz's Butterfly Attractor
chapters.tease: Three simple equations traced a never-repeating butterfly and proved perfect forecasts impossible.

chapters.title: The Mandelbrot Set
chapters.tease: A four-symbol formula, iterated by computer, revealed endless complexity and gave fractals a face.

chapters.title: Playfair's First Bar Chart
chapters.tease: A Scot short of data drew trade as lengths, and turned every comparison into a single glance.

chapters.title: Playfair's Pie Chart
chapters.tease: One divided circle showed an empire across three continents, and gave the world the part-to-whole chart.

chapters.title: Snow's Cholera Map
chapters.tease: One map of deaths around a water pump proved cholera was waterborne and founded modern epidemiology.

chapters.title: Nightingale's Rose Diagram
chapters.tease: Twelve wedges of blue showed ministers that soldiers died of filth, not bullets, and rewrote army medicine.

chapters.title: Minard's March on Moscow
chapters.tease: Six variables on one sheet turned Napoleon's lost army into a ribbon, setting the benchmark for data graphics.

chapters.title: Galton's Correlation Plot
chapters.tease: A tilted ellipse of family heights revealed regression to the mean and gave science correlation.

chapters.title: Booth's Poverty Map
chapters.tease: Seven colours painted on every London street proved poverty was vast, measurable and hidden behind main roads.

chapters.title: Du Bois's Data Portraits
chapters.tease: Hand-drawn charts at the 1900 Paris fair answered racist pseudoscience with data, colour and startling design.

chapters.title: The Sankey Diagram
chapters.tease: Drawing energy as bands of varying width exposed where engines wasted fuel, and how every system leaks.

chapters.title: Tukey's Box Plot
chapters.tease: Five numbers in a pencil-drawn box let anyone compare distributions at a glance and spot the outliers.

chapters.title: Leonardo's Vitruvian Man
chapters.tease: Leonardo fitted one body into a circle and a square, and made proportion the emblem of the human.

chapters.title: Leonardo's Exploded Views
chapters.tease: By pulling a machine apart on paper, Leonardo showed how to build what you have never seen built.

chapters.title: The Brookes Slave Ship
chapters.tease: A cold deck plan packed with human figures made the slave trade impossible to un-see.

chapters.title: Monge's Descriptive Geometry
chapters.tease: Two flat views, plan and elevation, became the universal language every engineer still speaks.

chapters.title: Watt's Indicator Diagram
chapters.tease: An engine drew its own portrait, and the area inside the loop measured the work it did.

chapters.title: Lovelace's Note G
chapters.tease: A table of operations for a machine that did not exist became the first published computer program.

chapters.title: The Blueprint
chapters.tease: Sunlight and iron salts let one drawing become a hundred exact copies, and big engineering scaled up.

chapters.title: The Wright Flyer Patent
chapters.tease: A patent figure of a twisting wing claimed control of the air, and started a decade of lawsuits.

chapters.title: The Apollo Mission Profile
chapters.tease: One sketch of leaving the mothership in lunar orbit made a Moon landing possible within the decade.

chapters.title: The IKEA Instruction Sheet
chapters.tease: Wordless flat-pack drawings let millions of strangers build furniture in any language.

chapters.title: The Turing Machine
chapters.tease: A tape, a head and a table of rules defined what computing is, a decade before computers existed.

chapters.title: The First Flowchart
chapters.tease: Boxes, branches and loops let programmers see a program's logic before a single instruction ran.

chapters.title: Von Neumann Architecture
chapters.tease: Putting the program in the same memory as the data gave almost every computer since its basic shape.

chapters.title: Shannon's Communication Model
chapters.tease: Five boxes separated meaning from signal, measured information in bits and founded the digital age.

chapters.title: Logic Gate Symbols
chapters.tease: A D, a shield and a bubble turned Boolean algebra into circuits anyone could draw, and build.

chapters.title: Baran's Distributed Network
chapters.tease: Three sketches of dots and lines showed that a mesh with no centre survives what a star cannot.

chapters.title: The ARPANET Map
chapters.tease: Four circles and five lines on a scrap of paper were the whole internet, and its first map.

chapters.title: Chen's Entity-Relationship Diagram
chapters.tease: Boxes for things and diamonds for links gave business and programmers one picture of their data.

chapters.title: The OSI Seven Layers
chapters.tease: A stack of seven boxes lost the protocol wars, then became the language every network engineer speaks.

chapters.title: Berners-Lee's Web Proposal
chapters.tease: A sketch of bubbles linked by labelled arrows proposed the World Wide Web, and its boss called it vague.

chapters.title: Cajal's Neuron Drawings
chapters.tease: Ink drawings of single brain cells proved the nervous system is built of separate neurons.

chapters.title: Ebbinghaus's Forgetting Curve
chapters.tease: One man memorising nonsense for years turned memory into something that could be measured.

chapters.title: Freud's Iceberg
chapters.tease: A picture Freud never drew became the world’s shorthand for a mind mostly hidden from itself.

chapters.title: Penfield's Homunculus
chapters.tease: A grotesque little man draped over the brain showed that the body is mapped onto the cortex.

chapters.title: The Prisoner's Dilemma Matrix
chapters.tease: Four boxes showed how two rational players can reason their way into an outcome both hate.

chapters.title: Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
chapters.tease: A pyramid its author never drew became the most familiar picture of human motivation.

chapters.title: Bloom's Taxonomy
chapters.tease: A ladder of six thinking skills changed how the world writes exams, lessons and learning goals.

chapters.title: The Johari Window
chapters.tease: Four panes gave a name to the blind spot and made feedback a skill teams could practise.

chapters.title: Kahneman and Tversky's Value Curve
chapters.tease: A lopsided S-curve showed that losses hurt more than gains please, and rewrote economics.

chapters.title: The Dunning-Kruger Curve
chapters.tease: Two flat lines and a famous fake mountain made overconfidence the most shared idea in psychology.

chapters.title: McCallum's Railroad Organisation Chart
chapters.tease: The first organisation chart was drawn to stop trains colliding, and it made the modern corporation thinkable.

chapters.title: Marshall's Supply and Demand Cross
chapters.tease: Two crossing lines became the first picture most people ever see of how a market sets a price.

chapters.title: The Gantt Chart
chapters.tease: Bars on a calendar made lateness visible at a glance and became the grammar of every project since.

chapters.title: The Deming PDCA Cycle
chapters.tease: A four-part wheel taught post-war Japan, then the world, that quality is a loop, not a finish line.

chapters.title: The Ishikawa Fishbone
chapters.tease: A fish skeleton made whole teams hunt for causes together, and became a basic tool of quality everywhere.

chapters.title: The SWOT Matrix
chapters.tease: Four boxes made strategy something any team could start in an afternoon, for better and for worse.

chapters.title: The BCG Growth-Share Matrix
chapters.tease: Stars, cows, dogs and question marks taught boards to manage businesses as a portfolio of cash.

chapters.title: Porter's Five Forces
chapters.tease: Five arrows moved strategy from beating rivals to understanding the structure of a whole industry.

chapters.title: The Diffusion of Innovations Curve
chapters.tease: A bell curve of who adopts new things, and when, became the map of every product launch and public campaign.

chapters.title: The Business Model Canvas
chapters.tease: Nine boxes on one poster replaced the fifty-page business plan and gave start-ups a shared language.

chapters.part: Charts for a Planet on the Edge
chapters.title: The Keeling Curve
chapters.tease: A wobbling line drawn from Hawaiian air proved that the carbon from our chimneys stays in the sky.

chapters.part: Charts for a Planet on the Edge
chapters.title: Moore's Law Plot
chapters.tease: A handful of dots on a log scale became a sixty-year roadmap for the computer industry.

chapters.part: Charts for a Planet on the Edge
chapters.title: The Gartner Hype Cycle
chapters.tease: One curve with no data gave boardrooms a shared language for boom, bust and the slow climb to usefulness.

chapters.part: Charts for a Planet on the Edge
chapters.title: The Hockey Stick Graph
chapters.tease: A thousand years of temperature in one picture made modern warming impossible to call normal.

chapters.part: Charts for a Planet on the Edge
chapters.title: The Planetary Boundaries
chapters.tease: Nine wedges round a green circle turned 'sustainability' into a dashboard with red lines on it.

chapters.part: Charts for a Planet on the Edge
chapters.title: Raworth's Doughnut
chapters.tease: A ring with a floor and a ceiling challenged economics' oldest picture: the line that only goes up.

chapters.part: Charts for a Planet on the Edge
chapters.title: Warming Stripes
chapters.tease: A chart with no numbers, axes or labels became the most recognised image of climate change on Earth.

chapters.part: Charts for a Planet on the Edge
chapters.title: Flatten the Curve
chapters.tease: Two humps under a dashed line explained a pandemic strategy and changed billions of people's behaviour.

chapters.part: Charts for a Planet on the Edge
chapters.title: The Transformer Architecture
chapters.tease: One block diagram from a translation paper became the blueprint for ChatGPT and the AI boom.

chapters.part: Charts for a Planet on the Edge
chapters.title: Korzybski's Map and Territory
chapters.tease: Five words and a strange pegboard diagram warned that every map, model and chart leaves the world out.
